access.title: Face access interactive planner
access.lead: Explore a YenShow access system with the YS AC-07 face terminal and YS-K2704X four-door controller.
access.diagram_hint_scenario: Highlights show the devices and signals used

face.title: YS AC-07 Professional Face Recognition Access Terminal
face.desc: This 7-inch touchscreen terminal supports face and contactless card authentication, with Wiegand, RS-485, and TCP/IP interfaces. A separate-controller setup requires a compatible reader mode to send credentials to the controller.
face.note: In direct-control mode, the terminal authorizes access locally, operates the lock relay, and accepts door contact and exit button inputs. Verify the firmware, reader mode, and interface when pairing with a controller.

controller.title: YS-K2704X Four-Door Access Controller
controller.desc: The YS-K2704X is the main controller in the YS-K2708X eight-door system. It has four lock outputs and four inputs each for door contacts and exit buttons. It authorizes access locally using incoming credentials and downloaded permissions and schedules.
controller.note: The YS-K2708X pairs one YS-K2704X with two YS-K2M002X door modules. The planner uses the four built-in door channels. Verify reader channels, interfaces, and firmware for two-sided identification.

lock.title: Electric lock
lock.desc: The door control device switches the lock circuit with a relay. An unlock output and actual door opening are separate events. The contact reports the door state.
lock.note: Select locks based on door type, electrical load, power-loss behavior, and the approved fire and egress design.

platform.title: YSOP Central Management Platform
platform.desc: YSOP is the management layer in this example. Confirm which interfaces and devices handle people, face templates, access rights, and event retrieval.
platform.note: The dashed purple line is a proposed management link. Deployment may use middleware and depends on YSOP version, licensing, and device compatibility.

power.title: Device power & UPS
power.desc: Size supplies for each terminal, controller, and lock to their specifications and load. The lock is powered through its specified control circuit.
power.note: Check voltage, peak current, runtime, and lock behavior on power loss. Verify the fire linkage while the system is on backup power.

exit.title: Exit button (REX)
exit.desc: For normal exit, the button sends a request to an input on the controller or integrated terminal. That device then controls the lock.
exit.note: Plan emergency release and mechanical egress separately according to the approved design, including doors with two-sided identification.

sensor.title: Door contact
sensor.desc: Reports actual door position to the controller or integrated terminal input. The device can use this state to detect forced or held-open doors.
sensor.note: Use the corresponding credential and authorization events to identify the person. The contact records door position.

fire.title: Fire safety linkage
fire.desc: The red link represents an approved hardware safety circuit acting on the lock. Integration depends on the door, lock power-loss behavior, and approved design.
fire.note: Verify lock behavior, mechanical egress, and event monitoring for each door under the site fire plan.

valid.title: Authorized staff access
valid.desc: The terminal recognizes the person and the controller checks door and schedule permissions before unlocking.
steps: The terminal matches the face and sends the credential
The controller checks door rights and schedule
The controller actuates the lock relay
The contact reports when the door changes state
valid.platform: Can receive an access granted event
valid.label: Granted
valid.note: Access events record authorization while the contact separately records the door position.

unknown.title: Unenrolled face fails recognition
unknown.desc: The example terminal has no matching enrolled face.
steps: The terminal compares the face with local templates
No valid match is found
The terminal sends no valid credential for this attempt
unknown.platform: Depends on terminal failure event support
unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.note: The face terminal performs the recognition in this scenario.

door.title: Credential valid, door unauthorized
door.desc: The controller receives a valid credential without access rights for this door.
steps: The terminal recognizes the person and sends the credential
The controller checks rights for this door
The controller denies access
door.platform: Can receive a door permission denial
door.label: Wrong door
door.note: The controller checks the access rights already downloaded to it.

time.title: Outside the authorized schedule
time.desc: The person has access rights for this door, but the time is outside the configured schedule.
steps: The terminal recognizes the person and sends the credential
The controller checks door rights and the schedule
The controller denies access outside the schedule
time.label: Wrong time
time.note: The controller uses its local clock and downloaded schedule.

offline.title: Management network down, local access active
offline.desc: The example assumes powered devices, a working reader link, and preloaded face data and access rights.
steps: The YSOP management connection is interrupted
The terminal matches locally and sends the credential
The controller checks its local rights and unlocks
Events can be recovered on reconnection if the integration supports it
offline.label: Offline
offline.sensor: Can continue to report door state
offline.note: Offline access requires valid local rights, enrolled credentials, and a working reader link.

fire.title: Fire linkage active
fire.desc: The approved hardware safety circuit acts on the lock when it receives the fire signal.
steps: The fire system issues the linkage signal
The safety circuit acts on the lock as designed
Occupants follow the approved egress route
fire.lock: Releases or changes state as designed
fire.platform: Depends on fire or access event integration
fire.label: Fire
fire.note: The red path shows the hardware linkage. Lock action depends on the selected lock and approved egress design.

reader.name: YS AC-07 Professional Face Recognition Access Terminal
reader.note: Verify model, firmware, reader compatibility, and template capacity for each direction.

controller.name: YS-K2704X Four-Door Access Controller

controller.note_integrated: Verify two-sided reader pairing and whether a secure door control unit is needed.

lock.name: Electric lock set

lock.note: Double doors, leaf type, lock style, and fire rules can change quantity.

sensor.note: Mounting and leaf structure need a site survey.

exit.basis: Check normal exit buttons, independent emergency release, and mechanical egress for each door.
exit.note: Two-sided identification still requires approved egress.

psu.name: Device power supplies / UPS
psu.basis: Size by voltage, current, zones, and backup time
psu.note: Check terminal, controller, and lock supply specifications and fire linkage under backup power.

network.name: Switches and network equipment

fire.note: Confirm wiring and component counts during the site survey.

product_links.platform: View the YSOP Central Management Platform

plan_notes.separate: Based on four built-in door channels per YS-K2704X. Multi-site plans show a minimum. Confirm door counts by site, interfaces, and installation locations.
plan_notes.separate_both: Allow two face terminals per door. Verify the entry and exit reader interfaces, compatible firmware, and available reader channels before sizing controllers.

cctv.title: CCTV architecture & storage
cctv.lead: Explore YenShow cameras, PoE switching, NVR recording, and YSOP viewing. Estimate storage from bitrate and retention.
cctv.diagram_click_hint: Boxes are clickable: select a device to see its role and data path
cctv.diagram_hint_record: Highlight = recording stream from IPC to NVR
cctv.diagram_hint_live: Highlights show how YSOP streams live video
cctv.diagram_hint_remote: Highlights show the path from camera to remote viewer

all.title: YenShow CCTV architecture
all.desc: YenShow IP cameras capture and encode video. PoE switches power cameras and carry streams. The NVR records and plays back footage, and YSOP VMS can centralize compatible streams, devices, and events.
points: Separate front-end, network, and back-end roles
Distinguish NVR recording from YSOP management
Confirm YSOP and device compatibility
all.note: Arrows show video direction. The NVR branch records video and the YSOP branch serves viewers.

record.title: Recording path from IPC to NVR
record.desc: Encoded streams travel from cameras through the switching fabric to the recorder and land on local or validated storage.
points: Confirm average and peak bitrate per camera
Check NVR inbound bandwidth, channels, and bays
Plan retention days and usable space after fault tolerance
record.note: The NVR need not share a cabinet with cameras; switch and uplink design must match distance and traffic.

live.title: Centralized live monitoring
live.desc: This example shows YSOP pulling streams from compatible cameras via the core network for authorized live viewing.
points: Validate ONVIF or vendor protocols
Size multi-view decode and bandwidth needs
Scope which cameras each role can see
live.note: An NVR can also supply streams where supported. Confirm device and platform compatibility and licensing.

remote.title: Secure remote viewing
remote.desc: Camera streams reach YSOP over the local network. Authorized users view them through a protected remote connection.
points: Prefer VPN or protected proxy/access layers
Control roles and account access
Assess uplink bandwidth and audit logs
remote.note: Do not expose NVR management ports to the public internet. Remote designs need security and product validation.

ipc.title: YS 2CD3141G2E-LIU 4 MP Smart Hybrid Light Fixed Dome Network Camera
ipc.desc: Supports 4 MP video, infrared and white-light illumination, person and vehicle detection, and H.265+ compression. It can receive PoE power and send video over the network.
points: Fixed lens field of view and mounting location
Recording resolution, frame rate, and bitrate
Illumination, PoE, and site conditions
ipc.note: Use the average bitrate for the selected recording settings in the estimator.

poe.title: YS 3T0310HP-E_HS 8-Port 100 Mbps Unmanaged Hi-PoE Switch
poe.desc: Six PoE ports and two Hi-PoE ports connect cameras. Gigabit RJ45 and SFP provide uplinks, and the switch has a 110 W PoE budget.
points: Per-port power and total PoE budget
Uplink type and aggregate video bitrate
Switch count for the site layout
poe.note: Plan VLANs, routing, and access control on the selected core network equipment.

core.title: Core network
core.desc: Aggregates edge switches, NVR, and YSOP traffic over copper or fiber depending on scale.
points: Aggregate and peak traffic
VLAN, routing, and access control
Redundant links and management
core.note: Shared uplinks need total bitrate and failover traffic sized carefully.

nvr.title: YS-7604NI-K1/4K 4-Channel 1U K/C Series 4K Network Video Recorder
nvr.desc: Records and plays back video from up to four IP cameras, with support for H.265+, H.265, H.264+, and H.264.
points: Camera count and input bandwidth
Drive bays and supported drive capacities
Recording retention and backup requirements
nvr.note: Check recording channels, decoding capacity, and drive capacity separately.

vms.title: YSOP Central Management Platform
vms.desc: YSOP VMS integrates compatible IP cameras and streams for live viewing and centralized management.
points: Interop and licensing
Multi-site and permission control
Events, alarms, and audit trails
vms.note: Scope follows shipping YSOP versions, licenses, and compatibility tests.

client.title: Operator client
client.desc: Authorized local or remote workstations use YSOP or NVR live view and playback.
points: Display and decode performance
Accounts, roles, and audit
Remote access hardening
client.note: Never share admin passwords publicly. Controlled remote access is not the same as exposing management ports.

cctv.nvr_capacity_note: The YS-7604NI-K1/4K shown supports four cameras. This calculator estimates site-wide storage. Size the recorder count or choose a higher-channel model based on total channels, input bandwidth, and drive bays. The estimate adds 20% planning headroom.

intercom.title: Smart video intercom
intercom.lead: Explore calling, answering, door release, and equipment planning with a YenShow door station, indoor station, and management station.

resident.label: Resident answer
resident.title: Resident answers and unlocks
resident.desc: The visitor calls from the door station. The resident checks the visitor and uses the indoor station to send a release command back to the door station.
steps: The door station calls the indoor station
The resident answers and checks the visitor
The indoor station sends the release command to the door station
The door station operates its lock relay
resident.unlock: Door station issued the release signal
resident.note: The command travels over the intercom network. The door station relay operates the physical lock circuit.

center.label: Center answer
center.title: Management center answers and authorizes release
center.desc: Staff answer on the management station and send a release command to the selected door station after checking the visitor.
steps: The door station calls the configured management station
Staff answer and check the visitor
The management station sends the release command back to the door station
The door station operates its lock relay
center.unlock: Selected door station issued the release signal
center.note: Confirm call routing, firmware, and video linkage for the selected deployment.

missed.label: No answer
missed.title: Call times out with no answer
missed.desc: If neither the indoor station nor the configured management station answers, the call leaves the lock state unchanged.
steps: The door station starts the call
The indoor station does not answer
If forwarding is configured, the management station also does not answer
The call times out and the door remains locked

access_link.label: Access link
access_link.title: Intercom unlock vs access boundary (TBD)
access_link.desc: This example assesses passing the door station's release request to a separate access control system.
steps: The indoor station user checks the visitor
The indoor station sends the request back to the door station
Verify the door station output and access controller interface
Use the specified access rules and lock circuit
access_link.note: The optional access control circuit handles the release request in this scenario. Confirm access policy, egress, and event logging in the system design.

outdoor.name: YS-KV6114-E1 IP Villa Door Station
outdoor.note: This example uses an IP/PoE layout. Confirm entry count, lock control, and station compatibility.

indoor.name: YS 6320-LE1W 7-inch Touchscreen Video Intercom Indoor Station
indoor.note: Plan extensions for each unit or answering point and check pairing and forwarding.

center.name: YS 9503 Management Station
center.note: Verify door station pairing, SIP registration, and call routing.

unlock.name: Unlock circuit
unlock.basis: Allows one lock circuit per door station, for {qty} circuits
unlock.note: The YS-KV6114-E1 supports two locks. Confirm the required circuit count and access control design.

network.name: Network / cabling
network.basis: Measure by building distance and topology
network.note: Do not infer from device count alone.

parking.title: LPR and parking management
parking.lead: Explore local plate recognition, barrier safety, and YSOP Parking integration using YenShow cameras, gates, and radar.

allow.label: Allowlist pass
allow.title: Allowlisted vehicle passes
allow.desc: The camera finds a valid match in its local allowlist and sends an open signal.
steps: Optional radar detects the vehicle and triggers capture
The camera captures and reads the plate
The camera checks its local allowlist
The camera sends the open signal through its relay
allow.note: This example uses the list stored on the camera. The integration can report events separately.

deny.label: Deny
deny.title: Non-allowlist denied
deny.desc: The gate starts closed and the plate fails the camera's local access check.
steps: The camera captures and reads the plate
The camera checks its local allowlist
With no valid match, the gate remains closed
deny.note: Configure separate rules for transient parking and visitor vehicles.

sensor.label: Safety radar
sensor.title: Radar detects an occupied gate zone
sensor.desc: The YS-TMG02 detects a person or vehicle while the barrier arm is raised.
steps: The radar checks the zone beneath the arm
The occupied signal reaches the gate safety input
The gate delays lowering as configured
After the zone clears, the gate resumes configured operation
sensor.note: The site safety circuit handles this path. Verify detection and operation on each lane.

review.label: Manual review
review.title: Exception plate needs review
review.desc: Staff check the integrated event and image when the plate read or match is uncertain.
steps: The camera captures and reads the plate
The plate or allowlist match needs review
Staff inspect the compatible event and image feeds
Staff confirm and follow the site process
review.note: Review functions depend on integration and authorization. At this stage the gate has received no open signal.

camera.name: YS-TCG405-E License Plate Recognition Camera

camera.note: Plate recognition and the local allowlist are onboard. Confirm installation points and lighting.

barrier.note: Confirm arm length, clearance, direction, and power-loss operation.

sensor.name: YS-TMG02 Barrier Gate Anti-Collision Radar
sensor.basis: Allow one set per lane for {lanes} lanes
sensor.note: Verify detection coverage and site safety operation.

allowlist.basis: Assess centralized integration for {people} allowlisted plates

booked.label: Booked check-in
booked.title: Booked check-in and optional credentials
booked.desc: Verifying an appointment creates a visit record. This example also includes optional badging and temporary access.
steps: Find the valid appointment
Verify the visitor and complete check-in
Create an open visit record
Issue a badge and temporary access if configured
booked.note: Badge issue and temporary access are separate optional steps after check-in.

walkin.label: Walk-in desk
walkin.title: Reception-assisted walk-in check-in
walkin.desc: Staff confirm the visit, complete check-in, and arrange an escort.
steps: Reception registers the walk-in
Confirm the host and reason for the visit
Complete check-in and create a visit record
Arrange a staff escort
walkin.note: Add badge or access issuance where required by site policy.

checkout.label: Exit close
checkout.title: Confirm departure and revoke temporary access
checkout.desc: Close the visit record and request revocation from the integrated access system.
steps: Confirm the visitor has left
Close the visit record
Request revocation where integrated
Collect a physical badge if issued
checkout.note: Verify access-system acknowledgement, expiry timing, and the visit record.

overstay.label: Overstay
overstay.title: Review overdue open visits
overstay.desc: Staff follow up on visits that remain open past their expected departure time.
steps: Check open visit records
Compare against expected departure
Have reception or security verify visitor status
Record departure or update the visit
overstay.note: Configured notifications can alert staff to overdue visits.
